# AGENTS.md — sha2lato

sha2lato is a self-hosted "agent box": Kimaki (Discord → OpenCode 2) + the
ui-ux-pro-max skill in one Docker image, with a DinD sidecar so the agent can
build and run project images. Multi-arch CI on GitHub + Forgejo, SSH deploys,
weekly CVE-fresh rebuilds. Public repo (MIT), fork-friendly.

Deploying the box rather than developing it? Point your agent at `docs/agent-setup.md` — a setup guide written to be executed by agents.

## Conventions for agents working in this repo

- **Line endings + exec bits:** LF everywhere; authored on Windows, runs on
  Linux. Shell scripts must be committed executable (`100755`) — from Windows
  use `git add --chmod=+x`; CI lint guards enforce it.
- **Secrets:** never commit real `.env*` files, `secrets/ssh/` contents, age
  private keys, or `data/`. Only `*.example` files, `secrets/age/*.age` and
  `secrets/age/recipient` are committable. Personal values live in
  `secrets/*.env` and `compose/.env` (gitignored).
- **One custom image:** `agent/` is the only Dockerfile. Everything else is
  official images wired by `compose/docker-compose.yml`.
- **Impersonal compose:** keep it fork-friendly — no personal values; use
  `secrets/*.env` (env_file) and `compose/.env` (interpolation).
- **Supply chain:** every dependency is first-party (Docker Official images,
  official apt repos/installers) or pinned (`tag@digest`, versioned build
  args) — do not add unpinned third-party images without documenting the
  trade-off.
- **Commits:** Conventional Commits — `feat:`/`fix:`/`chore:`/`docs:` (scope
  optional), `!` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` trailer marks a major image release.
  release-please turns merges into version bumps; released `vX.Y.Z` tags are
  never re-pushed ([versioning.md](docs/versioning.md)).
- **Validate changes** (from repo root): `docker compose -f
  compose/docker-compose.yml config --quiet`; `test/lint-sim.sh` (full CI-job
  simulation — lint via the same job image + socket pattern CI uses; copy the
  wrapper command from its header); markdown links must resolve.
- **Verify + review:** every change gets the review cycle (fresh lenses)
  before commit; external claims — CLI flags, APIs, upstream syntax — are
  confirmed against current upstream docs, not memory.
- **Docs:** main `README.md` is marketing-flavored; `docs/*.md` are practical
  and scoped. Update the docs index when adding a doc. Diagrams use Mermaid
  (renders natively on GitHub and Forgejo).
- **Knowledge graph:** when `graphify-out/graph.json` exists, use
  `graphify query` / `path` / `explain` before broad grepping. After code
  edits run `graphify update .` (free); after doc edits run
  `graphify extract . --backend deepseek --token-budget 10000` and
  `graphify label .` — the token budget is load-bearing: the default 60k
  packs the whole docs corpus into one LLM call and returns thin per-file
  coverage, which the extractor's shrink guard then refuses to write. The
  guard still trips on LLM variance (same command, fewer nodes): check the
  node diff and pass `--allow-partial`, or rebuild into a scratch `--out`
  dir and swap `graph.json`. If the graph is absent, skip it silently.
- **Config UX:** convention over configuration — the only required value is
  the bot token; every knob has one override point (`secrets/.env.agent` via
  `deploy/configure.sh`); users never edit compose/Dockerfile.
- **Long Docker builds / validations:** run them in separate subagents
  (parallel when independent) so verbose build logs stay out of the main
  context; have them report compact pass/fail summaries and sizes.

## Sharing diffs

In-chat diffs are the default. `critique --web "<title>"` uploads to the
self-hosted instance only when `CRITIQUE_WORKER_URL` is set (operator sets it
in `secrets/.env.agent` or the compose-UI env editor, then recreates the
agent). Unset or empty falls back to the third-party `critique.work` — keep
diffs in chat then.

## Current state

The box is complete and review-gated: agent image (Kimaki + OpenCode 2 +
ui-ux-pro-max + ponytail + graphify + the box tools: critique, tuistory, bun,
playwright CLI + chromium deps, gh), compose stack (agent + DinD + optional
local Whisper via the `whisper` profile, explicit volume names), secrets + age
overlay, GitHub + Forgejo CI (multi-arch, weekly rebuild, fork-safe), host
bootstrap/update/configure scripts, and scoped docs. Kimaki 1.5 is the runtime
(coordinator opt-in via `KIMAKI_COORDINATOR=1`, `kimaki diagram`,
local-Whisper client); the weekly rebuild tracks `KIMAKI_VERSION=latest`.
A docs website (`website/`, Holocron) renders from the same `README.md` +
`docs/*.md` and deploys to Cloudflare Workers when the CF secrets are set
(optional, fork-safe; upstream instance live at `sha2lato.elkodr.com`);
`docs/commands.md` is the command reference and `docs/agent-setup.md` the
agent-executable setup runbook.
`AGENT_PACK` uses `pack[@version]` — `agents-opencode` (default; runtime npm
latest) / `superpowers` (latest git tag) / `none`; exact pins supported.
`PONYTAIL=1` and `GRAPHIFY=1` default on; `GRAPHIFY_EXTRAS=openai` defaults on
so graphify's semantic pass can use `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY`.
Agent commits use a baked identity (`sha2lato agent`) and can be SSH-signed
with `GIT_SIGN=1`. Public on GitHub; CI green; multi-arch image on GHCR.
Forgejo CI is wired but the runner leg is deferred.

# Graphify usage

`graphify` turns a project into a queryable knowledge graph. Code is parsed locally with tree-sitter AST — deterministic, no model calls, nothing leaves the machine. Prefer it over grepping and file-by-file reading on anything beyond a handful of files.

## Build / refresh

- Build: `graphify extract .` — add `--code-only` to stay fully offline (skips docs/images that would need a model pass).
- Communities + report: `graphify cluster-only .` writes `GRAPH_REPORT.md` (god nodes, communities, suggested questions) and the interactive `graph.html`.
- Refresh incrementally after changes: `graphify update .`
- Everything lands in `graphify-out/` (`graph.json` is the graph itself; `cache/` makes re-runs incremental).

## Query the graph (prefer over re-reading)

- `graphify query "<question>"` — scoped subgraph for a plain-language question
- `graphify path "<A>" "<B>"` — how two things connect
- `graphify explain "<name>"` — one node and its connections
- Every edge is tagged `EXTRACTED` (explicit in the source) or `INFERRED` (derived) — you always know what was read versus guessed.

## Rules of thumb

- First contact with a repo of more than a few dozen files, or before a broad refactor: build the graph, then read `GRAPH_REPORT.md`.
- Ask graph queries before grepping; fall back to plain search for exact strings.
- Keep `graphify-out/` out of git — add it to the project's `.gitignore`.
- Worktrees: the graph is per-checkout. Build or update it inside the worktree you are working in.
- The CLI is baked into this box. Run `graphify --help` for the full command set (PR dashboard, wiki export, git hooks, MCP server).

# sha2lato website

Documentation site for sha2lato — [Holocron](https://holocron.so) (Vite plugin) deployed to Cloudflare Workers.

The pages in `src/` are thin wrappers: each imports the real markdown from `../README.md` or `../docs/*.md`, so GitHub, Forgejo, and the site all render one source. **Docs content lives in `docs/`, never here.**

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm install` | install dependencies (lockfile is committed) |
| `npm run dev` | dev server at http://localhost:5173 |
| `npm run build` | production build (worker + assets) |
| `npm run preview` | serve the production build locally |
| `npm run deploy` | build + `wrangler deploy` (needs `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` + `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`) |

## Dependency overrides

`package.json` `overrides` force two patched transitive deps — `katex` (via
`mermaid`) and `postcss-selector-parser` (via `@tailwindcss/typography`) —
because neither advisory has an in-range fix upstream. Drop each override once
`@holocron.so/vite` pulls a patched range on its own.

## Layout

- `docs.json` — site name, colors, fonts, navigation (groups + page slugs)
- `global.css` — theme tokens; Holocron picks it up automatically from the project root
- `src/*.mdx` — one wrapper per page (frontmatter + `import Doc from '../../docs/<name>.md'`)

# CI/CD

Two pipelines, one goal: build the agent image for **linux/amd64 + linux/arm64**, publish it to a registry, and deploy it to your host over SSH. Neither pipeline needs a runner you don't already have.

| Pipeline | File | Runs on | Publishes to | Deploys |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GitHub | `.github/workflows/` | GitHub's free hosted runners (public repo) | GHCR (`ghcr.io/<owner>/sha2lato-agent`) | SSH → `deploy/update.sh` |
| Forgejo | `.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml` | **your existing act_runner** | your Forgejo container registry | SSH → `deploy/update.sh` |

Both run lint + build (multi-arch) + deploy, plus a **weekly rebuild** (Monday 03:17 UTC) that republishes `:latest` with fresh base layers and deploys it, keeping hosts CVE-fresh without code changes. The GitHub pipeline builds each architecture on its own native runner; the Forgejo pipeline builds both on one runner with QEMU (see [runner requirements](#forgejo-runner-requirements)). SemVer releases are cut separately — [versioning.md](versioning.md).

## GitHub pipeline

- **`ci.yml`** — on push to `main`, version tags (`v*`), manual dispatch: runs **`lint`** (shellcheck + hadolint + actionlint, concurrently, in pinned containers) and the reusable **`build.yml`** **in parallel**, then calls **`deploy.yml`** (main only) once both pass.
- **`build.yml`** — reusable, native multi-arch → GHCR: a matrix job per architecture (`ubuntu-26.04` / `ubuntu-26.04-arm`, no QEMU) builds and pushes by digest **with `mode=max` provenance and SBOM attestations**, runs a **smoke test on the pushed image** (arch + version stamp, via the entrypoint, offline), then a **Trivy vulnerability gate** that fails the leg on fixable CRITICALs (`--ignore-unfixed`, so CVEs without an upstream patch don't red the build). The `merge` job validates the digests and assembles the multi-arch manifest with the tags: `latest`, `sha-…`, and on version tags `X.Y.Z` / `X.Y` / `X`. A failed gate leaves an untagged digest, so neither a broken nor a critically-vulnerable image is tagged. Serialized per ref (`concurrency: image-publish-…`) so a weekly rebuild and a push can't interleave into a rollback.
- **Hosted arm64 runners are free on public repos.** A *private* fork needs a paid plan or a self-hosted arm64 runner for the `linux/arm64` leg ([runner reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners)).
- **`deploy.yml`** — reusable, **self-skipping**: if `DEPLOY_SSH_HOST` isn't configured it logs a notice and succeeds (forks stay green). Serialized with `concurrency: deploy`.
- **Docker Hub mirror (optional)** — after the manifest is created, `merge` copies the same tag set to `docker.io/<DOCKERHUB_USERNAME>/sha2lato-agent` when both `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` + `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` repo secrets are set (self-skipping otherwise, so forks stay green). Because `build.yml` is a reusable workflow, only `GITHUB_TOKEN` is inherited — the two secrets are declared under `workflow_call.secrets` and passed by both callers (`ci.yml`, `rebuild.yml`); a manual `workflow_dispatch` of `build.yml` cannot receive repository secrets, so it never mirrors. Partial config (one of the pair set) fails the run instead of silently skipping. Docker Hub applies pull rate limits to anonymous consumers — GHCR does not.
- **`release.yml`** — release automation: [release-please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please) watches `main`, opens a release PR from Conventional Commits, and on merge creates the `vX.Y.Z` tag + GitHub Release. Because `GITHUB_TOKEN`-created tags don't trigger push workflows, it then dispatches `ci.yml` at the tag to publish the semver image tags. Scheme, pinning, bootstrap: [versioning.md](versioning.md).
- **`website.yml`** — optional docs website: builds `website/` and deploys it to Cloudflare Workers when `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` + `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` are set (self-skipping otherwise — forks stay green; [website.md](website.md)).
- **`rebuild.yml`** — the weekly cron: build + deploy, no code change required.
- **`renovate.json`** — Renovate opens PRs for base-image and action updates and SHA-pins Actions (`helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests`). Linter images referenced inside `run:` blocks are not tracked — see "Linter pinning".

**Secrets to set** (repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions): `DEPLOY_SSH_HOST`, `DEPLOY_SSH_USER`, `DEPLOY_SSH_KEY`, optionally `DEPLOY_SSH_PORT`. `GITHUB_TOKEN` is automatic. Optional: `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` + `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` enable the Docker Hub mirror. See [secrets.md](secrets.md).

## Forgejo pipeline

- On push to `main`, version tags, the weekly cron, and manual dispatch: **`lint` and `build` (multi-arch) run in parallel**, then `deploy` waits for both. Publishing is not lint-gated (same trade-off as GitHub); the host rollout is. The deploy step has the same self-skipping behavior.
- The Forgejo build emulates arm64 via QEMU on your one runner; GitHub uses native runners (see below). Website: the docs build + Cloudflare deploy job is independent of lint (it self-skips its deploy) and only runs on `main`.
- **Releases:** push a `vX.Y.Z` tag yourself (release-please runs on GitHub only) — this pipeline builds the semver tags. Scheme + pinning: [versioning.md](versioning.md).
- **Registry:** your Forgejo instance's built-in container registry. Set the two `forgejo.example.com` placeholders in the workflow to your host, and add repo secrets `REGISTRY_USERNAME` + `REGISTRY_TOKEN` (a Forgejo token with package write access).
- Override platforms on manual dispatch via the `platforms` input (e.g. `linux/amd64` to skip the heavy QEMU arm64 leg).
- **Action versions:** this pipeline stays one major behind GitHub on purpose — the newer action majors (checkout v7, docker/* v4–v7) run on Node 24, which needs an `act_runner` build with Node 24 support. Upgrade here once your runner has it; until then, keep the older pins. The GitHub pipeline also has no Docker Hub mirror and no per-arch smoke gate.

### Forgejo runner requirements

The pipeline runs on **your** act_runner, so unlike GitHub's hosted runners, the environment must be set up. Reference setup (exactly what this repo's workflow expects):

1. **A label the workflow targets.** The workflow uses `runs-on: linux`. Check your runner's labels in Forgejo → *Site Administration → Runners* (or repo *Settings → Actions → Runners*) and change `runs-on:` to match if needed.
2. **Socket whitelist for job containers.** In the runner's `config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   container:
     valid_volumes:
       - /var/run/docker.sock
   ```
   The workflow then requests the socket per job (`container.volumes`), so only jobs that need Docker get it.
3. **A job image with the tools, all from official sources.** The workflow pins `node:24-bookworm` (Docker Official, by digest) and installs Docker CLI + buildx from Docker's official apt repo in a ~30 s setup step. Everything else (node, git, bash, ssh, curl) ships in the image.

**Alternative job image:** `catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest` (digest in the workflow header comment history) is the community-standard act image — used by nektos/act itself — and bundles docker CLI + buildx + node + tooling, so the setup step can be dropped. Trade-off: a single-maintainer community image (MIT, 5M+ pulls) vs first-party sources. Either works; pick your trust model.

**Alternative socket strategies** (from Forgejo's official docs):

- `container.docker_host: 'automount'` in the runner config — mounts the host socket into *every* job container automatically. If you switch to this, **remove `container.volumes` from the workflows** (mounting the same path twice is an error).
- A `docker:dind` **service** per job (see Forgejo's "Utilizing Docker within Actions" guide) — best isolation, more setup.
- Worst case, per the Forgejo docs: mounting the host socket into jobs gives jobs access to **all host containers** — acceptable for a personal build runner with trusted workflows; for multi-tenant setups prefer dind.

**Notes:**

- With the socket-request approach, a job **must not** use `-v $PWD:…` mounts for tools like linters — a container created through the host socket resolves paths against the **host** filesystem, where the job workspace doesn't exist. This repo's lint steps pipe files via **stdin** instead (see any `lint` step). Same pattern works if you write your own workflows.
- Forgejo Runner **never updates already-downloaded images** — another reason everything here is pinned by digest.
- If `uses:` actions fail to resolve, check your instance's `DEFAULT_ACTIONS_URL` (`app.ini`): the default (`data.forgejo.org`) hosts the `actions/*` and `docker/*` mirrors these workflows use.
- Prefer a quick self-test? Run the **`runner-check`** workflow (manual dispatch) — it executes the exact Docker requirements of the real pipeline.

## Deploys (both pipelines)

The deploy step SSHes to your host and runs `deploy/update.sh`:

```
git pull --ff-only        # the host's checkout (default /opt/sha2lato)
# mode-aware — the script detects it from compose/.env:
#   build-on-host      → docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml build
#   pull-from-registry → docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml pull
docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml up -d --remove-orphans
docker image prune -f
```

- The host's git **`origin`** is the pull source — point it at whichever remote you treat as canonical (Forgejo or GitHub). Both pipelines can deploy the same host; deploys are serialized per workflow.
- **Modes:** `deploy/update.sh` reads `compose/.env` and either rebuilds on the host (`sha2lato-agent:local`) or pulls the registry image (any other ref) before recreating the stack. CI deploys assume the pull-from-registry mode. See [configuration.md → Deployment modes](configuration.md#deployment-modes).
- **Host-key hardening (optional):** the workflows pin the host key with `ssh-keyscan` at deploy time (trust-on-first-use). For stricter setups, store the host key in a repo secret and replace the `ssh-keyscan` line in `deploy.yml` / `.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml`.
- If the host has local changes, `git pull --ff-only` fails loudly — that's intentional.
- Override the checkout location with `SHA2LATO_DIR` (used by both `bootstrap-host.sh` and `update.sh`).

## Freshness strategy (CVE hygiene)

Component-by-component map — upstream repo, license, pin location, update lane: [upstreams.md](upstreams.md). This section explains the CI machinery behind it.

| Layer | How it stays fresh |
|---|---|
| Base image + system packages | Weekly rebuild pulls the newest `node:26-trixie-slim` and apt state; both pipelines republish `:latest` and deploy |
| Image version | SemVer releases from Conventional Commits (release-please + `release.yml`); the weekly rebuild moves only `:latest` + `:sha-…`, released `X.Y.Z` tags stay frozen — [versioning.md](versioning.md) |
| kimaki / ui-ux-pro-max-cli / tuistory / bun / playwright (npm) | Installed `@latest` at build time — the weekly rebuild refreshes them. Build args can pin versions for reproducible builds instead |
| critique CLI (GitHub release tarball) | **Runtime lane:** the entrypoint installs the newest release into the volume on every container start (`CRITIQUE_VERSION` env var pins it; sha256-verified from the release's own `.sha256` asset). Not baked — offline starts use the newest cached copy, and a cold volume with no network leaves `/diff` without a backend until a start succeeds |
| agents-opencode pack (npm) | Runtime-fetched by the entrypoint, not baked: bare `AGENT_PACK=agents-opencode` tracks npm latest on every container start; pin `agents-opencode@x.y.z` to lock the version (fetched with lifecycle scripts disabled). Cached on the volume; offline starts use the cached copy — the log warns if it differs from a freshly pinned version |
| superpowers plugin (git) | Runtime-fetched by OpenCode from a git tag: bare = latest tag re-resolved each start; pin `superpowers@v7.0.0` for exactness |
| graphify CLI (pip `graphifyy`) | Pinned via `GRAPHIFY_VERSION` (manual bump); optional backends via `GRAPHIFY_EXTRAS` (default `openai` for the DeepSeek/OpenAI semantic pass; empty = core only). Installed into its own venv at build time |
| ponytail plugin (npm) | Pinned in the entrypoint (`PONYTAIL_SPEC`, default `@dietrichgebert/ponytail@5.3.2`); OpenCode fetches it on first start — bump the spec to update |
| OpenCode | Installed from the official v2 install script at build time (Kimaki requires ≥ 2.0.19; it never pins) |
| CI actions (`actions/*`, `docker/*`) | Renovate PRs (pinned to digests) |
| Docker images (base, dind, linters) | Renovate PRs for the reference tags; **linter images are additionally pinned `tag@digest`** — see below |
| Forgejo job image | Digest-pinned in the workflow; bump the digest to refresh |
| Host OS | `unattended-upgrades` enabled by `bootstrap-host.sh` |

### Linter pinning

The `lint` jobs run these images, pinned `tag@digest` (immutable):

| Tool | Pin (recorded at `ci.yml` time) |
|---|---|
| shellcheck | `koalaman/shellcheck:v0.11.0@sha256:61862eba…` |
| hadolint | `hadolint/hadolint:v2.15.1@sha256:32dac941…` |
| actionlint | `rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12@sha256:b1934ee5…` |

# Deploy with Docker Compose and management UIs

The base path is plain `docker compose` on the host — [hosting.md](hosting.md) sets it up and [configuration.md](configuration.md) covers every knob. This page covers the same stack under a **compose management UI**: [Arcane](https://getarcane.app), Dockge, Portainer, and similar all run the same compose file, so the two recipes and rules below apply to any of them. Arcane is the reference implementation — its concrete behavior is labeled **(Arcane)**.

## What stays the same

The **agent container is unchanged**: Discord `!` shell commands, the agent's own shell tool, DinD builds — the UI only decides who runs `docker compose up`. A UI **shell/exec tab** (Arcane: **Shell tab**, `containers:exec`) covers the host-CLI equivalents (`kimaki bot install-url`, `kimaki status`, `graphify …`).

## Recipe 1 — discovered project (keeps the repo checkout)

Mount the UI's projects directory (Arcane: `PROJECTS_DIRECTORY`) so the **parent of the repo checkout** is inside it (for example mount `/opt` with the checkout at `/opt/sha2lato`). Arcane scans nested folders, so `compose/docker-compose.yml` is discovered and all repo-relative paths (`../secrets/…`, `../agent`) resolve exactly as with a plain `docker compose`.

- Works in both [deployment modes](configuration.md#deployment-modes).
- Discovered projects can't be tagged in the UI (Arcane); confirm Up/Redeploy once on first use.

## Recipe 2 — self-contained project (no checkout on the host)

Create a project in the UI and paste this compose (registry mode). Put `KIMAKI_BOT_TOKEN`, `MACHINE_NAME`, `AGENT_PACK`, `PONYTAIL`, `GRAPHIFY` (and optionally `CRITIQUE_WORKER_URL` for self-hosted diff uploads — see [configuration.md](configuration.md)) in the project's **environment editor** (Arcane: **Environment Configuration (.env)**) — workflow packs fetch at first start (network needed once), and `AGENT_PACK` takes an exact pin when you want one (`agents-opencode@3.1.2`, `superpowers@v7.0.0`). For git-over-SSH, create `secrets-ssh/` **on the host** (in Arcane's Projects Directory): `chmod 700` the folder, `chmod 600` the keys, plus `known_hosts` — SSH refuses group/world-readable keys, and the read-only mount means the container can't fix perms (Arcane's Workspace is fine only for `known_hosts`). Optional commit signing: add a dedicated `signing_key` the same way and set `GIT_SIGN=1` ([usage.md](usage.md) → Commits from the agent). Recipe 2 pastes the agent + dind services only; for on-box voice transcription, also add the optional `whisper` service, its volume, `COMPOSE_PROFILES=whisper`, and the `KIMAKI_WHISPER_*` values from [configuration.md → Local Whisper](configuration.md#local-whisper-optional).

> ⚠️ **The token then lives in the UI's store.** Arcane keeps project `.env` files in its own database — anyone with Arcane UI access can read them — and may include them in backups or exports. Treat that entry as a secret, **never** point a Push Git Sync or an export at it, and prefer **Recipe 1** (the token stays in the host's gitignored `secrets/.env.agent`). Same rule as [secrets.md](secrets.md): secrets never reach a repository.

```yaml
name: sha2lato
services:
  agent:
    image: ghcr.io/YOUR_USERNAME/sha2lato-agent:latest
    # or pin a release: :1 (minor stream), :1.4 (patch stream), :1.4.2 (frozen)
    # — see docs/versioning.md
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      DOCKER_HOST: tcp://docker:2376
      DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY: "1"
      DOCKER_CERT_PATH: /certs/client
    volumes:
      - agent-data:/data
      - dind-certs:/certs:ro
      - ./secrets-ssh:/root/.ssh:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "sh", "-c", "kimaki status --data-dir \"${KIMAKI_DATA_DIR:-/data}\""]
      interval: 60s
      timeout: 15s
      start_period: 60s
      retries: 3
  dind:
    image: docker:29-dind
    restart: unless-stopped
    privileged: true
    command: ["--host=tcp://0.0.0.0:2376", "--tlsverify"]
    networks:
      default:
        aliases:
          - docker
    environment:
      DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR: /certs
      DOCKER_HOST: tcp://localhost:2376
      DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY: "1"
      DOCKER_CERT_PATH: /certs/client
    volumes:
      - dind-certs:/certs
      - dind-data:/var/lib/docker
volumes:
  agent-data:
    name: sha2lato-agent-data
  dind-certs:
    name: sha2lato-dind-certs
  dind-data:
    name: sha2lato-dind-data
```

## Rules for UI-managed installs

- **One owner per stack.** If a UI manages the stack, do **not** set `DEPLOY_SSH_*` (the CI deploy job self-skips) and do **not** run `deploy/update.sh` — update from the UI (Arcane: **Redeploy** — pull + recreate — or **Auto Updates**). CI still builds and publishes images.
- **Explicit volume names** (`sha2lato-agent-data`, …) are set in both recipes: Arcane leaves explicitly-named volumes alone on project rename, so your data can't be copied or orphaned by a UI rename.
- **Paths must stay inside the project folder.** Arcane rejects compose path entries that point outside it; Recipe 2 exists precisely because the repo compose uses `../` paths.
- **Requirements:** a standard Docker daemon — privileged DinD does not work on rootless Docker or Podman; Compose ≥ 2.24 / Docker Engine 25+.
- **First start:** run `kimaki bot install-url` in the agent's shell tab (Arcane: **Shell tab**), authorize the bot, then restart the agent container.
- **Git Sync (Pull, Arcane):** set **Compose File Path** to `compose/docker-compose.yml` (Recipe 1 layout) and enable **Sync Files**; secrets live in the UI's `.env`/Workspace — synced files are read-only.

# Configuration

**Convention over configuration:** out of the box, the only value you *must* provide is your **Discord bot token**. Everything else has a default, every default has exactly one override point, and you never edit `compose/` or the `Dockerfile` for normal use.

## Easy mode: `./deploy/configure.sh`

On the host (after `bootstrap-host.sh`, or any checkout):

```bash
./deploy/configure.sh             # interactive: asks token, machine name, pack, worktrees
./deploy/configure.sh --show      # print current values
./deploy/configure.sh --non-interactive --token <t> --machine <m> --pack agents-opencode
```

It writes `secrets/.env.agent` + `compose/.env` (re-runs keep your current values as defaults), then just:

```bash
docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml up -d
```

## The two files

| File | From template | Holds | Committed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `secrets/.env.agent` | `secrets/.env.agent.example` | runtime config: bot token, pack, worktrees, optional keys | ❌ (chmod 600) |
| `compose/.env` | `compose/.env.example` | which image to run + optional compose profiles (`COMPOSE_PROFILES`) | ❌ |

Everything else in the repo is impersonal — fork-safe by design ([secrets.md](secrets.md)).

| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` | empty | optional model keys; `/login` in Discord is the recommended path |
| `SHA2LATO_AGENT_IMAGE` | `sha2lato-agent:local` | selects the [deployment mode](#deployment-modes): local tag = build on host, any registry ref = pull |

**Voice & TTS:** voice messages use a cloud key by default — set `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY` in `secrets/.env.agent` (above), or use `/transcription-key` in Discord (saved in `kimaki.db` on the volume). `kimaki tts` (spoken replies) always needs one of those keys.

### Local Whisper (optional)

To transcribe voice notes on this host instead of a cloud provider, enable the bundled [speaches](https://github.com/speaches-ai/speaches) service (MIT, CPU, pinned `0.8.3-cpu@sha256:21e3df06…`, profile `whisper`):

1. Enable the profile in `compose/.env`:

   ```ini
   COMPOSE_PROFILES=whisper
   ```

2. Point Kimaki at it in `secrets/.env.agent`:

   ```ini
   KIMAKI_WHISPER_URL=http://whisper:8000/v1
   KIMAKI_WHISPER_MODEL=Systran/faster-whisper-small
   ```

3. Start the stack and preload the model once (the first fetch downloads ~486 MB from Hugging Face into the `sha2lato-whisper-models` volume; later starts are local):

   ```bash
   docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml up -d
   docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml exec whisper \
     curl -fsS -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/models/Systran/faster-whisper-small
   ```

   The compose service sets `WHISPER__TTL=-1`, so the model stays in RAM between notes. (speaches 0.9 renames that knob to `STT_MODEL_TTL` — update the compose line on a major bump.)

Behavior and limits:

- **Only transcriber.** While `KIMAKI_WHISPER_URL` is set, Kimaki never falls back to OpenAI/Gemini — if the profile is off or the service is down, voice notes fail with an error in the thread. Enable the profile and the URL together.
- **Privacy.** Audio goes from the agent to `whisper` over the compose network; no port is published. The model weights are the only outbound fetch (Hugging Face, once). `kimaki tts` and live voice calls are unaffected and still use OpenAI/Gemini/ChatGPT.
- **Model.** `Systran/faster-whisper-small` (~486 MB, multilingual) is the recommended default; `base` is faster but weaker; `distil-*` is English-only. For Arabic and mixed-language notes, `small` is usable and `medium` is more accurate but ~3× slower — it can exceed Kimaki's 2-minute transcription cap on a weak CPU. Test with a real note before switching.
- **Updates.** The image is pinned `tag@digest` for reproducible builds: Renovate tracks pinned images on Mondays, and if the `-cpu` suffix is not picked up, bump tag + digest by hand. The model is a manual env change — edit `KIMAKI_WHISPER_MODEL`, preload the new ID, and prune the volume to remove old weights. The model ID resolves to a mutable Hugging Face repo (Kimaki's model field has no revision pin), so the weights are the one dependency not pinned by digest.

## Deployment modes

`SHA2LATO_AGENT_IMAGE` in `compose/.env` selects one of **two deployment modes**. Everything else — services, volumes, secrets — is identical.

| | `build-on-host` (default) | `pull-from-registry` |
|---|---|---|
| Value | `sha2lato-agent:local` | a registry ref, e.g. `ghcr.io/YOUR_USERNAME/sha2lato-agent:latest` |
| First start | `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml up -d --build` | `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml pull` then `up -d` |
| Updates | `./deploy/update.sh` rebuilds on the host | `./deploy/update.sh` pulls + recreates |
| Use when | first run, hacking on the image, no registry | the CI-published image: fast deploys, no build toolchain on the host, weekly CVE-fresh rebuilds |

- `deploy/update.sh` **detects the mode** from `compose/.env` and does the right thing; `--dry-run` prints the plan without executing.
- **Never run `up -d --build` in registry mode** — with both `image:` and `build:` set, it builds locally and tags over the registry ref instead of pulling.
- Switching modes = change the one line (`./deploy/configure.sh` asks), then `./deploy/update.sh`.
- Registry refs take semver releases too: `:1.4.2` (frozen release), `:1.4` / `:1` (moving streams), `:latest` (newest build, refreshed weekly) — see [versioning.md](versioning.md).

## Build-time (custom image)

The image lives in `agent/` and is parameterized for reproducible builds:

```bash
docker build \
  --build-arg KIMAKI_VERSION=1.0.0 \
  --build-arg UIPRO_VERSION=2.15.0 \
  --build-arg GRAPHIFY_VERSION=0.9.93 \
  --build-arg GRAPHIFY_EXTRAS=leiden,mcp \
  -t my-agent agent/
```

Defaults: `KIMAKI_VERSION=latest`, `UIPRO_VERSION=latest` (the weekly rebuild refreshes them), `GRAPHIFY_VERSION=0.9.93`; the tool args `TUISTORY_VERSION`, `BUN_VERSION`, `PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION`, `NPM_VERSION` also default to `latest` (the freshness lane — each rebuild re-resolves them; set an exact version for reproducible builds). One arg is a deliberate pin: `GRAPHIFY_VERSION`, because graphify feeds the baked usage guide and its venv extras, so majors are bumped by hand, not pulled in by a rebuild. The critique CLI is **not** a build arg at all: the entrypoint installs the fork's newest release into the volume on every start (sha256-verified against the release's own `.sha256` asset — a corruption/swapped-asset check, not an independent trust anchor), so a critique bump needs no rebuild; the [`CRITIQUE_VERSION` env var](#every-knob) pins one. `GRAPHIFY_EXTRAS` defaults to `openai`, which enables graphify's semantic LLM pass with a `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment; add `leiden` for community detection or `mcp` for the MCP server, or set it empty for core graphify only. Workflow packs are **not** build args — they're runtime config (`AGENT_PACK`), so changing pack or version never needs a rebuild.

## How changes apply

| Change | Apply with |
|---|---|
| any `secrets/.env.agent` value | `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml up -d` (container recreates; data volume untouched) |
| `compose/.env` image (mode switch) | `./deploy/update.sh` — it detects the mode and either rebuilds (build-on-host) or pulls (pull-from-registry) |
| workflow pack switch or version pin | same command — no rebuild; the entrypoint converges at start (new versions fetch on first start with network, then cache on the volume) |

State — projects, sessions, model logins — always lives in the `sha2lato-agent-data` volume. Configuration changes never touch it.

## Pack-managed defaults

The fetched `agents-opencode` pack ships a blanket `external_directory: "deny"` rule, which would block this box's cross-directory flows (new-project clones, `kimaki project add`). So the entrypoint **normalizes the global `external_directory` rule to `"ask"` on every start, whatever `AGENT_PACK` is set to**: it drops the legacy v1 `external_directory` entry — and the deprecated `permission` object itself once that was its only key — removes any `external_directory` entries from the v2 `permissions` array, and appends the canonical rules last — `{"action": "external_directory", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask"}` plus allows for the everyday working dirs `/tmp/opencode/*` (scratch), `/data/reports/*`, `/data/transcripts/*` and `/data/attachments/*` (OpenCode evaluates rules in order; the last match wins — the four allows follow the ask, so routine cross-session work needs no button while everything else still asks). Other rules (v2 array entries, unrelated v1 keys) are left untouched. The global `external_directory` namespace is **box-owned**: entries you add there — including denies like `~/.ssh/*`, in either format — are removed on every start; rules that must survive belong under `agents.<id>.permissions` (agent rules are evaluated after global rules). In Discord, permission asks appear as approve buttons in the thread; **Accept Always** saves a project-scoped allow rule, and agent-level permissions are the per-agent override lever. Everything else in the volume-resident `opencode.json` (plugins, other rules) is left untouched — only the global `external_directory` rule is re-normalized each start.

`PONYTAIL=1` also merges the pinned ponytail plugin spec into that same `opencode.json` (`plugins` array) — it layers on top of any workflow pack; `PONYTAIL=0` strips it again. `GRAPHIFY=0` removes the graphify usage guide from the volume's skills directory (the CLI itself stays available).

# Self-hosting your Discord bot

sha2lato uses a **self-hosted bot**: you create your own Discord application, so the bot identity, avatar, and permissions are entirely under your control. It takes about five minutes — plus one extra if you don't have a Discord server yet (step 0).

## What you need on Discord

Three things — only the last one is a machine you host; the rest are free and live on Discord's cloud:

- **A Discord server** — Discord's word for a *workspace* (the channel list in the app's sidebar). It is **not** a machine you run or pay for. Kimaki lives inside one: each project becomes a channel, each session a thread. A **dedicated server for agents** is recommended.
- **A bot application** — your bot's identity (name, avatar, token), created in the [Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications) in step 1. Free.
- **This box** — the sha2lato stack on your Linux host. It connects *out* to Discord: no inbound ports, nothing exposed.

> 💡 The server **is** the control surface — you drive the agent from it (phone or desktop), while the box does the work. No server yet? Step 0 takes under a minute.

## 0. Create your server (skip if you already have one)

1. In the Discord app, click **+** at the bottom of the left-hand server list → **Create My Own** → pick any option (**For me and my friends** is fine; skipping is fine too).
   *(If + is hidden under a long server list, scroll the list down to find it.)*
2. Enter a name (e.g. `Agents`) → **Create**.

You're now the server owner — which includes the **Manage Server** permission needed to add the bot in step 3. Reference: [How do I create a server?](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/204849977) *(Discord Help Center)*.

## 1. Create the application

1. Open the [Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications) → **New Application** → give it a name (e.g. `sha2lato`).
2. Go to the **Bot** tab.
3. **Enable “Message Content Intent”** — required for Kimaki to read your messages. Without it, the bot connects but ignores everything.
4. Make sure **Public Bot** matches your preference (leave it on if you want the shareable install link to work for others; off for yourself only).
5. Click **Reset Token** → copy the token. It looks like `MTAx…abc.def.ghi` (three dot-separated segments).

> ⚠️ The token is a full-access credential for the bot. Paste it only into `secrets/.env.agent` on the host — never into Discord, chat, or a commit.

## 2. Wire it into sha2lato

On the host:

```bash
cd /opt/sha2lato
# put the token in the agent env file
$EDITOR secrets/.env.agent
```

```ini
KIMAKI_BOT_TOKEN=MTAxYourBotTokenHere...
MACHINE_NAME=sha2lato        # the Discord category will be "Kimaki sha2lato"
```

Then start the stack:

```bash
docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml up -d
```

On first start, Kimaki reads the token **headlessly**, starts the bot, and saves the credential to the data volume (`/data/kimaki.db`) — later restarts work even if you remove the token from the env file.

## 3. Invite the bot to your server

Kimaki derives your bot's invite URL from the token:

```bash
docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml exec agent kimaki bot install-url
```

Open the printed URL in a browser logged into Discord, pick your server (a **dedicated server for agents** is recommended — see step 0), and **Authorize**. The URL requests exactly the permissions Kimaki needs:

> View Channels, Manage Channels, Send Messages, Send Messages in Threads, Create Public Threads, Manage Threads, Read Message History, Attach Files, Add Reactions — plus the `applications.commands` scope for slash commands.

## 4. Finish onboarding

Once authorized, Kimaki creates a category **`Kimaki <MACHINE_NAME>`** with a `#kimaki` channel and a **`Kimaki onboarding`** thread under it (the box starts Kimaki with coordinator mode off, so onboarding runs in a thread; `/toggle-coordinator` or `KIMAKI_COORDINATOR=1` turns channel chat on). If nothing appears within a minute (the bot was invited after its first boot), give it a nudge:

```bash
docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml restart agent
```

Then, in Discord:

1. Open the **`Kimaki onboarding`** thread under `#kimaki` and chat with the agent, or
2. Run **`/login`** in any channel — connect Claude Pro/Max, ChatGPT, Gemini, or an API key. Credentials are stored by OpenCode on the volume, so they survive restarts and image updates.

You are done. Send a message in `#kimaki` describing what you want, or tell the agent to clone a repo and add it as a project (see [usage.md](usage.md)).

## Access control

Kimaki only accepts messages from users with **one of**: Server Owner, **Manage Server**, **Administrator**, or a role named **`Kimaki`** (create it and assign it to trusted people — the recommended way for teams). Messages from other users are ignored.

To **block** someone (even an admin), give them a role named **`no-kimaki`**.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| Bot online but ignores all messages | Message Content Intent is off (Bot tab → enable → restart agent) |
| `kimaki bot install-url` says no bot configured | The agent hasn't completed its first start — check `logs agent`, ensure `KIMAKI_BOT_TOKEN` is set, `up -d` again |
| Category/channels never appear | `docker compose … restart agent` after inviting the bot |
| Logs show `install_url`/gateway events, agent restart-loops | `KIMAKI_BOT_TOKEN` is missing or malformed — the box fell back to Kimaki's shared-bot onboarding. Set the token, `up -d` |
| Token was leaked | Developer Portal → Bot → Reset Token → update `secrets/.env.agent` → `up -d` (new token replaces the saved one) |

More failure modes: [troubleshooting.md](troubleshooting.md).

# Optional: self-hosted GitHub runner

**Default: off.** The GitHub pipeline runs on GitHub's **free hosted runners** (unlimited for public repos), so most people need nothing here. Enable this profile when:

- your GitHub repo is **private** and you'd rather not burn the monthly hosted-runner minutes,
- you want CI builds to run on **your own hardware** (faster arm64, cache locality, no egress),
- or you're fully self-hosting and want the GitHub side to match your Forgejo runner setup.

## Setup

1. Create a **classic PAT** with `repo` scope at [github.com/settings/tokens](https://github.com/settings/tokens) (org runner: `admin:org`).
2. On the host:

```bash
cd /opt/sha2lato
cp secrets/.env.github-runner.example secrets/.env.github-runner
$EDITOR secrets/.env.github-runner      # REPO_URL + ACCESS_TOKEN
docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml --profile github-runner up -d
```

The runner registers itself as `sha2lato-github-runner` with labels `sha2lato,linux`.

## How this repo's workflows use it

The GitHub pipeline doesn't pin itself to your runner by default (hosted runners are the zero-config path). Two jobs would need editing:

```yaml
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, sha2lato]   # was: ${{ matrix.runner }}
  merge:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, sha2lato]   # was: ubuntu-26.04
```

A single x86_64 runner serves only the `linux/amd64` leg: the `linux/arm64` leg then fails in buildx unless the host has binfmt/QEMU registered (re-add `docker/setup-qemu-action` for that, at emulation speed). For both arches natively, add an arm64 runner and point the matrix's `linux/arm64` entry at its label instead. The `merge` job only needs registry access — it can stay on a hosted runner.

The runner service mounts the host Docker socket so jobs using `docker` (like this pipeline's lint+build) work — same trust model as your Forgejo build runner: treat it as a personal, single-tenant build machine.

## Notes

- The runner image ([myoung34/github-runner](https://github.com/myoung34/docker-github-actions-runner), GPL-3.0) is pulled from Docker Hub by you — it's not redistributed by this repo.
- To keep a profile-enabled runner running after `./deploy/update.sh`, set `COMPOSE_PROFILES=github-runner` in `compose/.env` so every compose invocation includes it.
- Unregistering: stop the container and remove the runner in the repo/org settings; its data volume (`sha2lato-github-runner-data`) can be deleted.

# Hosting

Two first-class paths. Both end at the same place: a Linux host running the compose stack, driven from Discord.

| | Path A — Bring your own Docker host | Path B — Azure VM |
|---|---|---|
| You have | any Linux box with Docker + SSH (VPS, home server, NAS with Docker) | nothing yet; want turnkey cloud |
| Setup | run `deploy/bootstrap-host.sh` | create VM (below) → same script |
| Networking | works behind NAT — the agent is **outbound-only** (Discord, registries); only SSH needs to be reachable by CI | NSG: allow SSH only |
| Cost | what you already pay | ~a few $/month (B2s-class) |

Either way you need: **SSH access**, **Docker Engine**, and (recommended) a **firewall**.

---

## Path A — Bring your own Docker host

**Requirements:** Linux (Ubuntu/Debian gets the most automation), Docker Engine 25+ (the compose file uses `env_file.required`, which needs Compose ≥ 2.24), `git`, and SSH access for CI deploys.

```bash
# on the host, once
git clone <your-fork-url> /opt/sha2lato     # or let the script do it
cd /opt/sha2lato
sudo ./deploy/bootstrap-host.sh            # installs Docker, ufw, unattended-upgrades; clones if needed
```

The bootstrap script is idempotent — safe to re-run. It:
1. Installs Docker Engine + buildx + compose plugins from **Docker's official apt repo**
2. Enables **ufw** with SSH-only inbound (see [Firewall](#firewall-and-ufw))
3. Enables **unattended-upgrades** (OS-level CVE hygiene)
4. Clones (or updates) the repo into `/opt/sha2lato` and creates `secrets/.env.agent` + `compose/.env` from the templates
5. Adds your sudo user to the `docker` group

Then follow the next steps it prints: fill in `secrets/.env.agent` ([discord-bot.md](discord-bot.md)), add git SSH keys ([secrets.md](secrets.md)), and start:

```bash
cd /opt/sha2lato
# build-on-host mode (the default). Using the CI-published image instead?
# see configuration.md → Deployment modes.
docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml up -d --build
```

### Updates

`deploy/update.sh` detects the [deployment mode](configuration.md#deployment-modes) from `compose/.env`, then either rebuilds on the host or pulls the registry image and recreates the stack. (`--dry-run` prints the plan.) Registry users can pin a release for change control — `:1`, `:1.4`, `:1.4.2` ([versioning.md](versioning.md)).

- **CI mode (recommended):** set your `DEPLOY_SSH_*` repo secrets and every push to `main` (plus the weekly rebuild) deploys automatically.
- **Manual:** `cd /opt/sha2lato && ./deploy/update.sh`
- The host's git `origin` is the pull source. Point it at whichever remote is canonical for you (Forgejo or GitHub):
  `git -C /opt/sha2lato remote set-url origin <url>`

---

## Path B — Azure VM (turnkey flavor)

Create an Ubuntu 24.04 LTS VM (any `Standard_B2s`/`B2ms`-class size; arm64 SKUs work too — the image is multi-arch):

1. **Create the VM.** SSH in with the key Azure generated.
2. **NSG (network security group):** allow inbound **SSH (22) only** — ideally restricted to your IP + your CI egress if you know it. Nothing else needs to be open: the agent makes outbound connections only.
3. **Bootstrap:**

```bash
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y git
git clone <your-fork-url> /opt/sha2lato
cd /opt/sha2lato
sudo ./deploy/bootstrap-host.sh
```

4. Continue exactly like Path A (fill env files → `up -d`).

**Azure-specific notes**

- Ubuntu cloud images ship with `ufw` installed but **inactive**; the bootstrap script enables it with SSH-only rules. If you rely on the NSG alone, you can remove the two ufw lines from the script — both layers are valid, choose one.
- Azure requires the VM's SSH key at creation; add that same public key (or a dedicated deploy key) to the host's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` for your CI user.

---

## Firewall and ufw

**ufw = Uncomplicated Firewall** — the standard Ubuntu/Debian front-end for Linux firewalls. `bootstrap-host.sh` runs:

```bash
ufw allow OpenSSH     # keep SSH reachable (you + CI deploys)
ufw --force enable    # default-deny everything else inbound
```

**Why this is enough:** the agent box needs **no inbound ports**. Kimaki connects *out* to Discord; Docker builds happen inside the stack; the kimaki lock port and DinD daemon are container-internal. The only inbound service is SSH.

**One caveat, worth knowing:** Docker manages its own iptables rules and **published container ports bypass ufw**. This stack publishes **zero ports**, so there is nothing to bypass — but if you later add a service with a `ports:` mapping, remember it will be reachable regardless of ufw, and firewall it at the NSG/cloud level instead.

**Non-standard SSH ports:** `bootstrap-host.sh` reads your sshd config (`sshd -T`, run as root) and keeps every listed port open alongside the standard `OpenSSH` rule — so enabling ufw cannot lock you out, even when run via `sudo` (which strips session environment variables). You can also pass an extra port explicitly: `sudo SSH_PORT=2222 ./deploy/bootstrap-host.sh`.

---

## Security notes

- **Privileged DinD:** the `dind` sidecar runs `privileged: true` — deliberately, since the agent builds and runs images. That is host-kernel-equivalent power: keep the host **single-tenant**, and control who can drive the agent with Discord roles ([discord-bot.md](discord-bot.md) → the `Kimaki` / `no-kimaki` roles).

## Sizing

| Workload | Suggested |
|---|---|
| Agent + DinD idling, light sessions | 2 GB RAM / 2 vCPU — workable |
| Comfortable daily driving, docker builds by the agent | 4 GB RAM / 2 vCPU |
| Heavy projects / many parallel sessions | 8 GB — plenty |
| Add the optional local Whisper service | +~1 GB RAM (small int8, kept loaded) + ~2–3 GB disk (image + model) |

Notes:

- CI builds do **not** run on this host (GitHub hosted runners / your Forgejo runner do that), so the box only needs to run the agent + DinD.
- Disk: count on ~5–10 GB base + whatever your projects and images use. DinD keeps its own image store (the `sha2lato-dind-data` volume) — `docker compose ... exec dind docker image prune -af` occasionally if it grows.
- arm64 hosts (e.g. Azure Dpsv5/Dplsv5) are fully supported — the published images are multi-arch, and arm64 builds inside DinD run natively.

# Secrets & the fork guide

**Design rule: nothing personal ever touches this repo.** Everything sensitive lives in gitignored `*.env` files and `secrets/` directories, documented by committed `*.example` templates. Forkers copy the templates, fill in their own values, and never inherit anyone's credentials.

## Where each secret lives

| Secret | Lives in | Committed? | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discord bot token | `secrets/.env.agent` (`KIMAKI_BOT_TOKEN`) → persisted to `/data/kimaki.db` on first start | ❌ (template `.env.agent.example` ✅) | agent container |
| Model credentials | `/login` in Discord → OpenCode data on the volume; optional provider API keys in `secrets/.env.agent` | ❌ | agent container |
| Git SSH keys (for repos the agent works on) | `secrets/ssh/` (mounted read-only at `/root/.ssh`) | ❌ | agent container |
| Which agent image to run | `compose/.env` (`SHA2LATO_AGENT_IMAGE`) | ❌ (template `.env.example` ✅) | docker compose |
| CI deploy key | `DEPLOY_SSH_*` repository secrets on GitHub/Forgejo | ❌ (never in repo) | CI pipelines |
| Registry credentials | `REGISTRY_USERNAME`/`REGISTRY_TOKEN` repo secrets (Forgejo) / automatic `GITHUB_TOKEN` (GitHub) | ❌ | CI pipelines |
| Docker Hub mirror (optional) | `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME`/`DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` repo secrets (GitHub), passed to the reusable `build.yml` by both callers | ❌ | CI pipeline |
| age overlay (optional) | `secrets/age/*.age` + `secrets/age/recipient` (encrypted + public key — **safe to commit**), private key stays in `~/.config/sha2lato/age.key` | ✅ for `*.age` and `recipient` | you, on any machine |

> If you deploy with a compose management UI like [Arcane](compose-ui.md) using its self-contained recipe, the bot token lives in that tool's project `.env` instead of `secrets/.env.agent`. The same rule applies: treat it as a secret, keep it out of any Git sync or export, and prefer the host-checkout recipe when you can.

## Runtime env files

```bash
cd /opt/sha2lato
cp secrets/.env.agent.example secrets/.env.agent
cp compose/.env.example compose/.env
```

**`secrets/.env.agent`** — required: `KIMAKI_BOT_TOKEN`. Optional: `MACHINE_NAME`, `KIMAKI_WORKTREES=1` (fresh git worktree per session), `KIMAKI_COORDINATOR=1` (channel coordinator instead of a thread per message), provider keys (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`) as an alternative to `/login`, `CRITIQUE_WORKER_URL` for a self-hosted critique instance (and `CRITIQUE_PASSWORD` to lock its links), `KIMAKI_WHISPER_URL`/`KIMAKI_WHISPER_MODEL` for on-box voice transcription (with `COMPOSE_PROFILES=whisper` in `compose/.env` — see [configuration.md](configuration.md#local-whisper-optional)).

```ini
# or: SHA2LATO_AGENT_IMAGE=forgejo.example.com/YOUR_USERNAME/sha2lato-agent:latest
```

## Git SSH keys (for the agent's projects)

The agent clones and pushes over SSH. Give it a dedicated key — **do not reuse your personal key**.

```bash
cd /opt/sha2lato
mkdir -p secrets/ssh && chmod 700 secrets/ssh
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "sha2lato-agent" -f secrets/ssh/id_ed25519 -N ""
chmod 600 secrets/ssh/id_ed25519
# pin the hosts so SSH never prompts inside the container
ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 <your-forgejo-host> github.com > secrets/ssh/known_hosts 2>/dev/null
```

Optional — **commit signing**: create a second, dedicated key and lock it down:

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f secrets/ssh/signing_key -N ""
chmod 600 secrets/ssh/signing_key
```

Register the **public** half — GitHub: Settings → SSH and GPG keys → **Signing Key** (verification only); Forgejo: added to your account it is a normal SSH key that *also* authenticates (push/read as you) — use a dedicated forge account for a clean agent identity. Then set `GIT_SIGN=1` in `secrets/.env.agent` ([usage.md](usage.md) → Commits from the agent). Keep it separate from `id_ed25519` — one key for pushing, one for signing; always `chmod 600` on the host (the container mount is read-only and cannot fix permissions). The key is passphrase-less (headless necessity): anyone who compromises the container can mint commits that verify as the agent identity — keep the host single-tenant.

Then add the **public** key (`secrets/ssh/id_ed25519.pub`) as a **deploy key** — separately on each host you use:

**Forgejo:** repo → *Settings → Deploy Keys → Add.* Enable write access if the agent should push (it usually should). Repeat per repository. *(For multiple repos, consider a machine/user key instead: Forgejo user → Settings → SSH keys.)*

**GitHub:** repo → *Settings → Deploy keys → Add deploy key.* Same write-access decision. *(For many repos: create a dedicated GitHub account or fine-grained PAT alternative — deploy keys are per-repo.)*

Verify from inside the container:

```bash
docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml exec agent sh -c 'ssh -T git@<your-forgejo-host> || true'
```

The `secrets/ssh/` directory is mounted read-only at `/root/.ssh`; the agent can use the keys but cannot modify them (that is intentional).

## CI deploy key

The pipelines deploy by SSH'ing to your host and running `deploy/update.sh`. Generate a dedicated key **on your workstation** and set:

| Secret (GitHub repo secrets / Forgejo repo secrets) | Value |
|---|---|
| `DEPLOY_SSH_HOST` | hostname or IP of the Docker host |
| `DEPLOY_SSH_USER` | SSH user (needs docker access — `root`, or a user in the `docker` group) |
| `DEPLOY_SSH_KEY` | **private** key contents (the whole `-----BEGIN…` block) |
| `DEPLOY_SSH_PORT` | optional, default `22` |

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "sha2lato-ci-deploy" -f ~/.ssh/sha2lato_deploy -N ""
ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/sha2lato_deploy.pub <user>@<host>
```

If the secrets are **not set**, the deploy jobs skip themselves with a notice — forks stay green without configuration.

## Optional: age overlay (encrypted backups you can commit)

Want your `.env` files backed up in the repo, safely? Encrypt them with [age](https://github.com/FiloSottile/age):

```bash
deploy/age.sh keygen      # creates ~/.config/sha2lato/age.key + secrets/age/recipient
deploy/age.sh encrypt     # secrets/.env.* → secrets/age/*.age  (committable)
deploy/age.sh decrypt     # restore on a new machine (bring your private key or AGE_KEYFILE env)
```

- The **private key never enters the repo** (`~/.config/sha2lato/age.key`, or wherever `AGE_KEYFILE` points). Back it up somewhere safe — it's the whole point.
- `secrets/age/*.age` and `secrets/age/recipient` are safe to commit (that's the design: forkers can encrypt *to* you, only you can decrypt).
- If you change your `.env`, re-run `deploy/age.sh encrypt` and commit the updated `.age` files.

## Never commit

Real `.env` files, `secrets/ssh/` contents, age private keys, or `data/`. The `.gitignore` blocks all of these — if `git status` ever shows one, something is wrong; stop and fix it before committing.

## Agent / bot

| Symptom | Likely cause → fix |
|---|---|
| Agent container **restart-loops**; logs show `install_url` / gateway events | `KIMAKI_BOT_TOKEN` missing or malformed in `secrets/.env.agent` — the box fell back to Kimaki's shared-bot onboarding. Set the token → `up -d` |
| Bot **online but silent** in channels | Message Content Intent disabled in the Developer Portal, or the channel doesn't belong to this machine. Check [discord-bot.md](discord-bot.md) + Kimaki's `no-kimaki`/role rules |
| Channel answers in the channel instead of opening a thread | Coordinator mode is on for that channel — the box default is off, so it comes from `/toggle-coordinator` or `KIMAKI_COORDINATOR=1`. `/toggle-coordinator` switches that channel back to thread-per-message; `/reset-coordinator` starts a fresh coordinator on the next message |
| Onboarding starts in the channel instead of a thread | `KIMAKI_COORDINATOR=1` is set in `secrets/.env.agent` — unset it and recreate the agent (`up -d`); the default onboards in a thread |
| No `Kimaki <machine>` category after inviting the bot | Onboarding retries on next start: `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml restart agent` |
| Cross-directory flows (cloning a new project, `kimaki project add`) **blocked with no approve prompt** | The global `external_directory` rule is not `"ask"` — a restart re-normalizes it: `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml restart agent`. The entrypoint also allow-lists the everyday dirs on every start — `/tmp/opencode` (scratch), `/data/reports`, `/data/transcripts`, `/data/attachments`; everything else asks. Inspect with `… exec agent jq '.permissions' /data/opencode/config/opencode/opencode.json` |
| Sessions stop responding | `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml exec agent opencode service restart` — Kimaki reconnects by itself |
| Need to restart just the bot | `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml exec agent kimaki restart` (sessions keep running) |
| Where are the logs? | `… exec agent kimaki logs` → path (`/data/kimaki.log`); follow with `--follow`. The file resets on every bot start |
| Running bare **`kimaki`** in a container shell **stops the bot and the container exits** | `kimaki` starts a bot and enforces one instance: before binding port 29988 it evicts the running one — SIGTERM to its supervisor, which is PID 1 here — so the container exits and `restart: unless-stopped` brings it back; in-flight turns are lost. Use a subcommand (`kimaki status` / `logs` / `restart`); if you must run bare `kimaki`, add `--if-not-running` so it cannot evict |
| `kimaki status` says **"not running"** while the bot is up | Host exec shells on images built before this ENV fall back to `~/.kimaki`: check with `… exec agent printenv KIMAKI_DATA_DIR` (empty = the running container predates the ENV — `up -d` after pulling) and add `--data-dir /data`. Agent-session shells get the var from kimaki's plugin; the container healthcheck passes the flag |
| Re-onboarding with `docker compose run -it agent kimaki --restart-onboarding` would touch the live data | The one-off shares `/data` but gets its own network namespace, so it cannot see (or evict) the live bot — it would race it on `kimaki.db` and overwrite `lock-token`. Stop the service first: `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml stop agent` → `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml run -it --rm agent kimaki --restart-onboarding` → `up -d` |
| Healthcheck reports **unhealthy** | `kimaki status` inside the container shows *why not running*; usually the same token issue as row 1 |
| `AGENT_PACK` / `PONYTAIL` / `GRAPHIFY` set but the feature isn't active | `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml logs agent \| grep entrypoint` — the convergence lines print on every start. `agents-opencode`: fetched to `/data/opencode/npm`; delete the marker `/data/opencode/config/.agents-opencode-installed` and restart to reinstall. `superpowers` / `ponytail`: OpenCode fetches the plugin on first start — needs network once. `graphify`: verify the CLI with `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml exec agent graphify --help` |
| A pinned pack version isn't what's running | The exact fetch needs network once: with a cold cache, an offline start logs `npm fetch failed` / `keeping the current spec` and the pack is skipped or runs at the cached version — restore connectivity, then `up -d` again. Cached packs and the npm cache live in `/data/opencode/npm` |
| `graphify: command not found` inside the container | Should not happen (the CLI is baked into the image) — rebuild the image; the entrypoint never removes it, only the usage guide |
| Bot online but auth/model errors, token looks correct | `secrets/.env.agent` may have Windows CRLF endings — values then carry a stray `\r`. Rewrite the file with LF endings (or re-run `./deploy/configure.sh`). |
| Agent commits fail with *"please tell me who you are"* | Update to a current image (`./deploy/update.sh` — the default identity ships in images built with it), or set `GIT_USER_NAME`/`GIT_USER_EMAIL` in `secrets/.env.agent` and `up -d` |
| `Permissions 0644 … too open` — SSH ignores the key | Fix on the host: `chmod 600 secrets/ssh/<key>` (the mount is read-only — the container cannot fix it) |
| `kimaki upload-to-discord` posts an empty message / drops attachments | Known issue on kimaki `<= 1.1.0`; current images bake the latest kimaki — rebuild/redeploy (`./deploy/update.sh`) and retest. Workaround meanwhile: copy files out via a shell or another transport |
| Kimaki is older than npm latest (`npm ls -g kimaki`) | Kimaki is baked at build time — rebuild/redeploy takes `KIMAKI_VERSION=latest`. Inside a live container `npm i -g kimaki@latest && kimaki restart` works but is lost on recreate |
| `npm install` skipped a project's native/build scripts | npm 12 (baked since the `NPM_VERSION=latest` lane) denies install-time lifecycle scripts by default. Allow the ones you trust: `"allowScripts"` in the project's `package.json`, or `npm i --allow-scripts=<pkg>` per command. Git deps need `--allow-git=all` / `npmrc allow-git=all`; URL tarballs `--allow-remote=all`. Pin `NPM_VERSION=11.x` to restore npm 11 behavior |
| `curl -6` / IPv6 connections fail from inside | Expected: the box has no IPv6 egress (IPv4-only container networking); dual-stack client issues cannot be reproduced from inside |
| `opencode upgrade` seems to have no effect | The running service keeps the old binary — restart it: `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml exec agent opencode service restart` (sessions survive; pending permission prompts are cancelled) |

## Voice / Whisper

| Symptom | Likely cause → fix |
|---|---|
| Voice note fails with `Whisper server at … not reachable` | `KIMAKI_WHISPER_URL` is set but the `whisper` profile is not running — `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml --profile whisper up -d`, and set `COMPOSE_PROFILES=whisper` in `compose/.env` so updates keep it. There is no cloud fallback while the URL is set |
| First voice note after setup times out (2-minute cap) | The model was downloading inside the request. Preload it once: `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml exec whisper curl -fsS -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/models/Systran/faster-whisper-small`; keep notes short on weak CPUs |
| Arabic / mixed-language note transcribes poorly | `small` is the multilingual baseline; switch `KIMAKI_WHISPER_MODEL` to `Systran/faster-whisper-medium` (better, ~3× slower; may hit the 2-minute cap on a weak CPU). `distil-*` is English-only |
| Out-of-memory or slow transcription | `WHISPER__COMPUTE_TYPE=int8` and `small`/`base`; raise host RAM; the service keeps the model loaded (`WHISPER__TTL=-1`) |
| Voice notes still hit a cloud API | `KIMAKI_WHISPER_URL` not set in the running container — check `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml exec agent printenv KIMAKI_WHISPER_URL`, then `up -d` after editing `secrets/.env.agent` |

## Docker-in-Docker (agent builds)

| Symptom | Likely cause → fix |
|---|---|
| `Cannot connect to the Docker daemon` inside sessions | DinD sidecar down or certs stale: `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml up -d dind` → re-run. If it persists, wipe the cert volume and recreate both: `down`, `docker volume rm sha2lato-dind-certs`, `up -d` (builds/images are in `sha2lato-dind-data`, unaffected) |
| Builds suddenly fail with TLS/cert errors | Same as above — the shared certs volume got corrupted; recreate it |
| `ECONNREFUSED` connecting to a compose service from the agent | The port is published to `127.0.0.1` inside DinD (bound in the sidecar's netns). Publish to `0.0.0.0` (`"5432:5432"`) and connect to `docker:<port>` — see [usage.md](usage.md) → Docker-based projects |
| Sidecar eats disk | Prune inside it: `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml exec dind docker image prune -af` (DinD has its own image store) |
| dind logs `containerd binary not found, starting embedded containerd` and `Running with experimental embedded-containerd mode` | Expected on `docker:29-dind`: the image intentionally ships no separate `containerd` binary, so dockerd runs its embedded containerd in experimental mode. Benign |
| dind logs `failed check for fsverity support` / `Failed to find nft tool` | Benign upstream startup checks — the host filesystem has no fsverity, and the image has no `nft` binary (dockerd's firewall falls back). No action |
| dind logs `healthcheck failed … Unavailable … only one connection allowed` | Embedded-containerd's single-client quirk: `docker info` queries containerd and can transiently collide under load. The compose healthcheck uses `docker version` (no containerd query), so container health no longer flaps on it. Build-time `calling snapshotter.Remove is forbidden` / content-store lock warnings are the same experimental-mode noise from BuildKit — harmless, builds complete |
| QEMU/multi-arch builds hang | arm64 via QEMU is slow — expected. GitHub CI builds each arch natively; the Forgejo workflow still emulates arm64. There, prefer fewer platforms or a native arm64 host |

Every versioned component this box pulls from upstream — what it is, where its version is controlled, and which update lane keeps it fresh. ## Update lanes (the short version)

| Lane | Covers | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| **Automatic** | CI actions + pinned Docker images (dind, optional runner, optional whisper) | merge Renovate PRs (Mondays); the whisper model is a manual env change, not an image |
| **Scheduled** | Floating build-time deps: base image, npm, apt, kimaki, ui-ux-pro-max, tuistory, bun, playwright, gh, OpenCode, Docker CLI | nothing on CI-deployed hosts — the weekly rebuild republishes `:latest` **and deploys it** (GitHub `rebuild.yml`; Forgejo: cron in `.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml`). | **Manual** | Deliberate pins: graphify CLI, ponytail default, linter + Forgejo job-image digests | bump the pin — workflow pins are commit-only; image pins also need a rebuild/redeploy |
| **Runtime** | Workflow packs, ponytail plugin + critique CLI — no rebuild at all | edit `AGENT_PACK` / `PONYTAIL_SPEC` / `CRITIQUE_VERSION` in `secrets/.env.agent` (or your compose UI's `.env` editor) + `up -d` to recreate — env files are re-read on recreate, not on a plain restart ([compose-UI users](compose-ui.md): **Redeploy**). ## Update everything (checklist)

1. **Merge Renovate PRs** — actions, docker images (dind, base, runner).
2. **Bump deliberate pins if wanted** — `GRAPHIFY_VERSION`, linter digests ([procedure](ci-cd.md#linter-pinning)), Forgejo job-image digest, ponytail default spec. Critique needs no bump: the entrypoint installs the newest release on each start (set `CRITIQUE_VERSION` in `secrets/.env.agent` to freeze one).
3. **Rebuild / redeploy** — `./deploy/update.sh` on the host; CI-deployed users get it from the weekly rebuild (GitHub `rebuild.yml` / Forgejo cron) or dispatch it manually; compose-UI users: **Redeploy**.
4. **Runtime packs** — bare values are already current (re-resolved at every container start); exact pins apply on the next start.
5. **Verify** — CI green, then watch the entrypoint convergence lines in the logs ([troubleshooting.md](troubleshooting.md)).

# Usage — day 2 from your phone The mental model: **channels are projects, threads are sessions**. Send a message in a project channel and Kimaki opens a **thread** with one OpenCode session working in that project's directory. Kimaki 1.5's channel **coordinator** is opt-in: set `KIMAKI_COORDINATOR=1` in `secrets/.env.agent` (then `up -d`) to make each channel one long-lived session that starts a thread per piece of work, or toggle it per channel with `/toggle-coordinator`. - A channel message opens a thread; `/new-session` starts another one. - `/toggle-coordinator` turns the channel chat on or off; `/reset-coordinator` starts a fresh coordinator on the next message. - Return to any thread anytime (search, `/resume`). - Everything the agent does (reads, edits, test runs, docker builds) happens on **your** host, inside the agent container and its DinD sidecar. ## First steps in Discord | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `/login` | Connect a model provider (Claude Pro/Max, ChatGPT, Gemini, API keys) — do this once | | `/model` | Switch the model for a channel or session (or `/-agent` shortcuts) | | `/agent` | Switch the agent/system prompt | | `/verbosity` | Tune how much the bot posts in a channel | | `/session-id` | Show the session ID + command to open it in the OpenCode TUI (if you run one on the host) | Long prompts are easier as **attachments**: tap `+` → “Send message as file”. ## Creating new projects (from Discord, no SSH needed) The agent has the `kimaki` CLI on its PATH inside every session. To add a project, just ask: > “Clone `git@your-forgejo-host:you/new-app.git` into `/data/projects/new-app` and add it as a project.” The agent runs the clone + `kimaki project add /data/projects/new-app` — and a **new channel appears** in your server. Brand-new (not yet existing) projects work too: > “Create a new project `scratch` in `/data/projects/scratch`, `git init` it, add a starter README, and add it as a project.” Requirements: SSH access to the git host (see [secrets.md](secrets.md)); git present (it is, in the image). ## Everyday workflows - **Queue work while the agent is busy** — end a message with `. queue` (or `/queue`); edit the Discord message later to update the queued text. Great from mobile: “run the full test suite and report back. queue” - **Ask a side question without derailing** — end with `. btw` (or `/btw`): forks the context into a new thread while the main run continues. - **Worktrees — isolated experiments** — `/new-worktree ` starts a session in a fresh git worktree (never touching your main checkout); `/merge-worktree` merges it back (rebase or squash). Make it automatic per channel with `kimaki channel worktrees on` (or `KIMAKI_WORKTREES=1` for all sessions). - **Review diffs on your phone** — `/diff` posts a shareable web diff URL of the session's changes. - **Tunnels — see your dev server from your phone** — ask the agent to run `kimaki tunnel -- ` (or `-p `); it prints a public URL you can open anywhere. Keep a tunnel alive in a named background session and read its output later via `tuistory` — e.g. `tuistory launch "kimaki tunnel -- pnpm dev" -s myapp-dev`, then `tuistory read -s myapp-dev` to grab the URL. - **Voice** — record a voice note (transcribed with your file tree by default, or on-box when the optional [local Whisper](configuration.md#local-whisper-optional) service is enabled); or join the **Kimaki voice** channel and talk. `kimaki --voice ` once to change the voice. - **Diagrams** — the agent renders Mermaid to a PNG with `kimaki diagram` and posts it; repo docs keep Mermaid source (GitHub/Forgejo render it), so don't commit the PNGs. - **Images & files** — attach screenshots/files to messages; the agent can also upload files back into the thread. - **Shell commands** — prefix a message with `!` to run it raw in the project folder (e.g. `! git status`). - **Routines — scheduled prompts** — ask for a cron-style routine (e.g. “every weekday at 8:00, summarize open PRs in this channel”) — great for morning digests from your phone. - **Sessions sleep & wake** — long-idle sessions are cheap; resume whenever. ## Feature support (baked tools) The box ships the full toolset — diff viewer, tunnels, background sessions, headless browser, and more — see [Baked-in tools & commands](commands.md) for the complete reference. Anything there is also runnable yourself with `! ` in a channel, or `docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml exec agent ` on the host. ## Access control Only the server owner, members with **Manage Server**/**Administrator**, or members with a role named **`Kimaki`** can drive the bot. A role named **`no-kimaki`** blocks anyone (even admins). See [discord-bot.md](discord-bot.md). ## Docker-based projects The agent has full `docker` (and `buildx`, `compose`) against the **DinD sidecar** — isolated from the host daemon. So it can `docker build`, `docker run`, spin up compose stacks, run test containers, and even multi-arch builds. Images live in the sidecar's own volume; if disk grows: ```bash docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.yml exec dind docker image prune -af ``` **Ports & service URLs (DinD).** Services published to `127.0.0.1` inside a project's compose bind in the **sidecar's own network namespace** — unreachable from the agent. Switching any of them later is the same one-line change + `up -d` — no rebuild; new pack versions fetch on first start (then cache on the volume). **Discord synergy:** Kimaki exposes the packs natively — agents appear as `/-agent` switches and commands as slash commands. Try `/plan-project`, `/execution-loop`, `/checkpoint` (agents-opencode), `/ponytail-review` (ponytail), or ask *“tell me about your superpowers”* (superpowers). For graphify, just say *“graph this repo first”* when a codebase is large or unfamiliar. **Worktrees — one owner only:** | Active pack | Worktree guidance | |---|---| | `agents-opencode` (or none) | Kimaki worktrees fully compatible — `KIMAKI_WORKTREES=1` or per-channel `kimaki channel worktrees on` | | `superpowers` | **Leave `KIMAKI_WORKTREES` unset** (and channel worktrees off) — Superpowers manages git worktrees itself as part of its branch lifecycle; the entrypoint warns if both are set | **Does this affect Kimaki?** No — Kimaki identifies sessions by its thread↔session mapping, not by filesystem layout, so sessions stay distinct no matter how git worktrees are managed. The only rule is worktree ownership (table above). With superpowers active, review changes through its branch/merge flow (`git log`, PR) rather than `/diff` on the main checkout — its work happens on its own branch. **Details:** - `agents-opencode` is fetched from npm on first start into `/data/opencode/npm` (on the volume — offline starts keep working afterwards) and installed into the global OpenCode config, all languages. Bare = npm latest, re-resolved every start; `agents-opencode@x.y.z` pins exactly. Verify in Discord: ask *“@orchestrator plan this”* or look for the slash commands. - **Cross-directory access:** on every start, the entrypoint normalizes the global `external_directory` rule to `"ask"` in OpenCode v2's `permissions` array — the fetched agents-opencode pack ships a blanket `"deny"` that would silently block documented flows that write outside the session's project directory (cloning new projects, `kimaki project add`). The four everyday dirs (`/tmp/opencode` scratch, `/data/reports`, `/data/transcripts`, `/data/attachments`) are additionally **allow-listed on every start**, so routine cross-session work needs no button; everything else still asks. In Discord, permission asks appear as **approve buttons in the thread**: **Accept Always** saves a project-scoped allow rule, and agent-level permissions are the per-agent override lever. - **Pack updates:** bare packs re-check for a newer version on every start; exact pins change only when you edit them. A version-tracked marker re-installs the pack files on the volume automatically. - `superpowers` is fetched from git by OpenCode; bare = latest tag re-resolved each start (offline keeps the current spec), `superpowers@v7.0.0` pins exactly (needs ≥ v6.4.1 on OpenCode v2).
